entities.summary: Burg Kreuzenstein is a castle near Leobendorf in Lower Austria, Austria. Burg Kreuzenstein is 265 metres (869 ft) above sea level. It was constructed on the remains of a medieval castle that had fallen into disrepair and was then demolished during the Thirty Years' War. Intended to be a family vault for the Wilczek family, it was rebuilt in the 19th century by Count Nepomuk Wilczek with money from the family's large Silesian coal mines. Kreuzenstein is interesting in that it was constructed out of sections of medieval structures purchased by the family from all over Europe to form an authentic-looking castle.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a unique example of a medieval castle reconstructed from salvaged structures across Europe, Burg Kreuzenstein provides insight into the cultural and economic practices of the Wilczek family during the 19th century. Its construction reflects the family's significant wealth, with an estimated €10 million spent on purchasing medieval structures.
